To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

students who are given a chance to learn statistics through discovery and inquiry, who are encouraged to think deeply about statistical ideas, and who have opportunities to reflect on their own thinking and to make their thinking public, will learn more than students who are given traditional instruction.

(1) Students learn better when they can relate what they are learning to what they already know; (2) students learn better when they have a chance to reflect on what they know; (3) students learn better if they can construct a mental model of what they are learning; (4) students learn better with a deep understanding of the concepts than with a shallow understanding; and (5) students learn better from active learning activities than from passive activities.
The cognitive theory of learning provides an excellent theoretical basis for understanding how students learn statistics and why some instructional approaches are more successful than others.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how students learn and how we might improve their learning by applying the principles of cognitive theory to the teaching of statistics.
the application of cognitive theory to statistics education.
the question: What can cognitive psychology teach us about how to teach statistics?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cognitive theory is an important source for the improvement of statistics education.
the application of cognitive theory to statistics instruction can provide a means for improving student learning and understanding of statistics.
the cognitive theory is very important for the students and teachers to understand and use it in their daily teaching and learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cognitive theory of learning can help to make sense of what is known about how people learn and how people teach, to explain why reform efforts work, to provide guidelines for implementing these reform efforts, and to generate new and effective instructional strategies.
cognitive theory can provide us with a powerful set of tools to improve our teaching.
the cognitive theory of learning provides a useful framework to guide instructional design decisions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
statistics education is a complex and dynamic system that requires a holistic approach to instructional design.

statistics instructors can use cognitive theory as a lens to view and interpret their students' learning experiences, and to design effective instruction that is grounded in theory and informed by research.
cognitive theory provides a powerful lens through which we can examine the design of statistics courses and the teaching of statistics.
